test.name: Extract assertions from the 1890 Ferber–Becker marriage index entry
test.description: FamilySearch index entry for the 1890 Hamilton County, Ohio marriage of William H. Ferber and Emma Becker ('Ohio, County Marriages, 1789-2016', ark:/61903/1:1:XZR1-JZP). Real record from the Ferber/Becker research (#799). Sparse index: names + year + county, no parents recorded.

input.user_message:
Extract assertions from this marriage record:

Ohio, County Marriages, 1789-2016 — FamilySearch index entry
ark:/61903/1:1:XZR1-JZP

Groom: Wm. H. Ferber
Bride: Emma Becker
Marriage year: 1890
Event place: Hamilton County, Ohio

(This index entry records no parents' names for either party.)

judge_context: Marriage year (1890) and place (Hamilton County, Ohio) are DIRECT evidence — stated on the record
Extract assertions for BOTH parties — Wm. H. Ferber (groom) and Emma Becker (bride)
Source classification should be DERIVATIVE — FamilySearch indexed transcription of the county register, not the register image

No parents recorded in this index entry — no parent assertions should be invented, and no negative-evidence assertion should be manufactured for the blank field either. record-extractor.md's "Negative evidence" section is explicit: negative evidence is about a PERSON expected-but-absent, never a blank FIELD on a person who is present, and a "No X recorded" value for an unrecorded optional field is over-extraction. The body's own test is whether the value NAMES the specific absent person (that section's `value` bullet — "never blank, never just 'absent'"); here it cannot, because the parents' names are exactly what the entry does not give. So: a value of the form "No parents' names recorded for groom <name> in this index entry" is the failure, and silence is correct. If a negative assertion IS created, it must still use record_role 'absent' and informant_proximity 'researcher'. Do not dock the skill for writing no negative assertion at all — that is the expected behaviour.

Informant: the parties are informants for their own facts (proximity 'self'), INCLUDING the marriage event itself (date, place) — they participated in the ceremony firsthand. The clerk and any officiant are RECORDERS, not the event's informant: do not credit or require 'official_duty' for the marriage date/place, and do not dock 'self'
'1890' is a year, not a full date — do not fabricate an exact day (the 10 Sep 1890 date lives only on the original register image, a separate record)
